realLife: A single perceptron is rarely used alone today, but it is the unit stacked into every neural network.
summary: One neuron: a weighted sum and a threshold, nudged only when it gets a point wrong.
headline: The smallest learner there is
overview: A perceptron adds up its inputs with weights, adds a bias, and says yes or no by the sign. When it misclassifies a point, it pushes the weights toward that point's label. When it is right, nothing changes.
If a straight line can separate the groups, this rule is guaranteed to stop making mistakes after a finite number of updates. If not, it keeps shuffling forever.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Choose XOR. No straight line separates the two diagonals, so the mistake bars never reach zero however many passes you allow.

check.question: What happens when a perceptron is trained on data no straight line can separate?
options: It keeps updating and never settles

data: Eighty points in 2D, labels 0 or 1. Weights start at zero. Each pass visits the points in the same order. The engine reproduces scikit-learn's Perceptron weights exactly after ten passes.
maths: $$\text{if } y_i\,(w^{\top}x_i+b)\le 0:\quad w\leftarrow w+y_i x_i,\quad b\leftarrow b+y_i\qquad(y_i\in\{-1,+1\})$$

If the data is separable with margin γ and every point has length at most R, the rule makes at most (R/γ)² updates (Novikoff, 1962). The bound says nothing about which of the many separating lines it finds.
code:
from sklearn.linear_model import Perceptron
m = Perceptron(max_iter=1000, tol=1e-3, random_state=0).fit(X, y)
m.coef_, m.intercept_
